Series::StatAccessor::pdist2¶

Back to Series::StatAccessor API Reference

Signatures¶

Series Series::StatAccessor::pdist2(const Series& other) const
Series SeriesStatProxy::pdist2() const
Series SeriesStatProxy::pdist2(const Series& other) const

What It Does¶

pdist2() computes the matrix of Euclidean distances between rows of two [points,features] inputs. On this accessor it is a naming companion to cdist(): the 2 refers to two point sets, not to squared distance.

For owner [m,d] and peer [n,d], result [m,n] has out[i,j]=sqrt(sum_k (owner[i,k]-peer[j,k])^2).

Calling Styles¶

left.stat.pdist2(right) and left.stat(right).pdist2() are equivalent. The second spelling uses a peer-bound SeriesStatProxy; it does not square the result or reverse operand order.

Example¶

auto left = pluss::make_series({{0.0, 0.0}, {1.0, 1.0}});
auto right = pluss::make_series({{1.0, 0.0}, {3.0, 4.0}});
std::cout << left.stat.pdist2(right) << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 5],
  [1, 3.6055513]]

The bottom-right value is sqrt((1-3)^2+(1-4)^2)=sqrt(13), not 13.

Example 2. The proxy form binds the second point table before selecting the method.

std::cout << left.stat(right).pdist2() << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 5],
  [1, 3.6055513]]

Use this form when a program passes around a peer-bound statistical proxy. For an immediate calculation, left.stat.pdist2(right) is shorter and equally clear.

Example 3. Compare pdist2() with a genuinely squared result.

auto distance = left.stat.pdist2(right);
std::cout << distance << "\n";
std::cout << distance.square() << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 5],
  [1, 3.6055513]]
pluss::Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 25],
  [1, 13]]

If an objective needs squared Euclidean distance, square the returned matrix explicitly. That makes both units and gradient scaling visible in the code.

Gradient¶

Both point sets participate in reverse mode. Each pair contributes opposite unit-vector sensitivities to its left and right points. Coincident points use a zero subgradient; see cdist for a complete both-sided reverse example.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • pdist2() does not return squared distances.

  • Both inputs must be rank 2 with matching feature widths and platforms.

  • Output shape is [left rows,right rows]; it is not a condensed triangular vector of within-table distances.

  • Use cdist() when that name communicates the operation more clearly to your readers; the accessor behavior is equivalent.

See Also¶

  • cdist: the same pairwise Euclidean distance contract.
